summary: Independent review reproduced the weak AOT validation and failed-set memory contamination on the prepared base. At the exact candidate commit, strict envelope/type/version/key/payload validation rejected the original and adversarial invalid artifacts, failed writes no longer contaminated memory, focused cache-key tests passed, and a fresh-process GPU cache round trip produced correct output.

tests.what_was_measured: The base accepted an unversioned CompiledArtifact pickle, accepted schema_version=True as a dictionary payload, retained an invalid payload in memory/disk, and retained a valid artifact in memory after cache-directory creation failed. This reproduced the original weak-validation behavior and the reported remaining contamination gap.
All 7 candidate regressions passed, including strict bool schema-version rejection and failed-set cache isolation.
Independent cases rejected raw legacy pickles and schema_version=True with RuntimeError; invalid-payload and I/O-failed set operations left no in-memory entry.
All 19 related cache-key and interface-completeness tests passed.

tests.command: FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/flydsl-review-j-799cd05b89b6-cache /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-799cd05b89b6/venv/bin/python examples/01-vectorAdd.py (twice in separate processes at candidate commit)
tests.what_was_measured: Both MI350X/gfx950 executions printed PASS against torch A+B; the persisted file was independently inspected as a dictionary containing artifact, cache_key, format=flydsl.compiled-artifact, and schema_version=1, and the second process exercised its persisted cache.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2 / torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4) executed vector addition twice with independent torch numerical comparison; both runs printed PASS.

native_rebuild_reason: The candidate changes only python/flydsl/compiler/jit_function.py, a Python test, and a prior report. No C++ or native compiler source changed, so the prepared rebuild command was not applicable. The runtime continued to use the image's pinned native extension while Python imported from /job/repo/python.
remaining_limitations: GPU execution was validated only on the assigned MI350X/gfx950; no claim is made for architectures unavailable in this job.
The schema logic itself is host-side Python and received direct regression/adversarial coverage; no native rebuild was needed or performed.

Pickle is deserialized before envelope validation, so this is compatibility/integrity validation rather than protection from malicious pickle input; hostile-cache security was not part of the reported contract.
